verifications.claim: "Apollo 2" was not an officially designated mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'There was no Apollo 2 or 3.' R2: 'no missions or flights were ever designated Apollo 2 and 3.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements in R1 and R2 confirm no official designation for Apollo 2.

verifications.claim: "Apollo 2" is the informal name for the uncrewed AS-202 suborbital flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'AS-202 (also referred to as SA-202 or Apollo 2) was the second uncrewed, suborbital test flight'
verifications.reasoning: R3 explicitly states AS-202 was also referred to as Apollo 2, implying informal usage.

verifications.claim: The AS-202 suborbital flight was launched on August 25, 1966.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: AS-202 was part of the Saturn IB test program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'third test flight of the Saturn IB' 'launched with the Saturn IB launch vehicle'
verifications.reasoning: R3 confirms it as a Saturn IB test flight.

verifications.claim: AS-202 successfully tested the Apollo command module’s heat shield.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'designed to test the heat shield by subjecting it to 260 megajoules per square meter' 'The success of this flight enabled...'
verifications.reasoning: R3 describes the heat shield test and overall mission success.

verifications.claim: AS-202 successfully tested the Apollo command module’s systems before human flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'first flight which included the spacecraft guidance, navigation control system and fuel cells' 'enabled the Apollo program to judge the Block I spacecraft and Saturn IB ready to carry men into orbit on the next mission, AS-204'
verifications.reasoning: R3 details systems tested and success qualifying for crewed flight.

verifications.claim: No mission was officially designated Apollo 2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'There was no Apollo 2 or 3.' R2: 'no missions or flights were ever designated Apollo 2 and 3.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation from R1 and R2.

verifications.claim: AS-202's mission goal was suborbital test of the Block I command/service module.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Suborbital test flight of a production Block I Apollo command and service module'

verifications.claim: AS-202 focused on heat shield endurance, guidance, and fuel cells.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'test the heat shield' 'first flight which included the spacecraft guidance, navigation control system and fuel cells'

verifications.claim: AS-202 used a Saturn IB launch vehicle.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'launched with the Saturn IB launch vehicle' 'third test flight of the Saturn IB'

verifications.claim: The AS-202 spacecraft was recovered in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'North Pacific Ocean' 'Recovered by USS Hornet' 'Landing site North Pacific Ocean'

verifications.claim: AS-202 reached an altitude of roughly 660 nautical miles.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.reasoning: Reference specifies 617.1 nautical miles, which significantly differs from 660 nautical miles even with 'roughly'; numbers must match precisely for the entity.

verifications.claim: After the 1967 Apollo 1 tragedy, NASA reordered the program's schedule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On January 27, 1967... killed... On September 11, 1967, numbering of the Apollo missions began with... Apollo 4.' R2: 'After the Apollo 1 tragedy... first Saturn V launch... would be known as Apollo 4.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe schedule and numbering changes post-tragedy.

verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe final numbering decision but do not mention any consideration of renumbering early missions.

verifications.claim: NASA decided to start with Apollo 4 for the first Saturn V flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first Saturn V launch, scheduled for November 1967, would be known as Apollo 4.'

verifications.claim: The officially recognized Apollo sequence jumped from Apollo 1 to 4.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'numbering... began with... Apollo 4... There was no Apollo 2 or 3.' R2: 'no missions or flights were ever designated Apollo 2 and 3.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm the skip in official numbering.

verifications.claim: AS-202 and AS-203 were never officially re-christened as "Apollo 2" or "Apollo 3" in the final record.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'There was no Apollo 2 or 3.' R2: 'no missions or flights were ever designated Apollo 2 and 3.' R3: 'also referred to as... Apollo 2' (implying informal)
verifications.reasoning: No official designation confirmed; R3 notes informal reference only.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'AS-202 was the third test flight of the Saturn IB, because a delay... pushed its launch past the July 1966 launch of AS-203.'
verifications.reasoning: R3 places AS-203 in the sequence of Saturn IB test flights.
